THE CLAIM UNDER TEST IS #59's OWN, NOT THE R5G6B5 EXPANSION THAT ALREADY LANDED. The Z/O suffix on a colour surface format names what the RASTER STORES into the pad bits, not a constant the texture unit substitutes on readback. #48 implemented the readback; that is exact on every pixel the raster drew and wrong on every pixel it did not. Arm B stamps the constant in glsl/psh.c, stops the blend unit overwriting it in vk/draw.c, and removes the readback swizzle from vk/texture.c.

WHY THE MODEL IS NOT A GUESS, and it needed no device. Surface format draws its scratch surface twice, once with the sampled alpha as coverage and once with alpha FORCED OPAQUE by the combiner. A readback constant can only ever change a sampled alpha: it cannot reach the forced half and cannot reach a colour channel at all. The X1R5G5B5 O and Z GOLDENS differ in that forced half on 16,384 of 16,384 px, every one a clean green +128 with R, B and A bit-identical -- a 1555 word's pad bit is the high bit of the word's second byte, and the test samples every surface through one LU_IMAGE_A8R8G8B8 stage, so two 1555 words are read as one texel whose byte 1 is green. The two tests' guest code differs only in the format register. Re-derivable with docs/testing/surface_pad_write_side.py, which exits non-zero if the read-side model survives and which FAILS when pointed at the 4-byte pair, so it is answering rather than agreeing.

L1, THE DISCRIMINATING LEG. Surface_format/Fmt_X8R8G8B8_O8R8G8B8 = 0, bit-exact. It cannot reach 0 under the read-side model at any scoping whatsoever: at the tip it carries 59,183 differing px of which 58,159 are OUTSIDE the two quad rectangles, every one of them the single transition (32,32,32,255) -> (0,0,0,255), which is the test's own CPU memset of the 640x480 scratch region showing through where a constant the raster never wrote there had overwritten it. 88% of what this test samples is never rendered. The value 0 is not forced by my patch -- my patch decides what bytes are stored, the GOLDEN decides whether that matches silicon -- and it is the number a composite of two existing arms' real pixels (post-#59 inside the quad rectangles, pre-#59 outside them) scores against the golden: 0 differing px, max delta 0 in every channel.

L2, THE CONTROL ON THE SAME PAIR, and it is labelled a control rather than evidence. Fmt_X8R8G8B8_Z8R8G8B8 = 0. It is 0 today and must stay 0, but it is 0 BY LUCK: its pad constant is zero and the memset background is zero too, so the two models coincide. This is the third time in this issue that the Z variant has passed for that reason. It is worth registering because it fails if the stamp picks the wrong constant, if the blend unit clobbers alpha, or if padAlphaMode fires on the wrong format -- it is not worth citing as evidence for the model.

L3, THE FORMATS WITH NO PAD BITS. Fmt_A8R8G8B8 = 0 and Fmt_R5G6B5 = 0, and Fmt_B8 and Fmt_G8B8 bit-identical between the arms. pgraph_glsl_surface_pad_alpha_mode returns NONE for all four, so a move here means the mode table or the synthetic blend field reaches a format it has no business reaching.

L4, THE DELIBERATELY OUT-OF-SCOPE PAIR. Fmt_X1A7R8G8B8_{Z,O}1A7R8G8B8 bit-identical. Their X bit sits above seven bits of REAL alpha that we store at 8-bit precision, and vk/constants.h has already measured their readback as (X << 7) | (stored >> 1) over 32,755 invertible px, so stamping the pad bit without the 7-bit requantisation would be half a fix. They are excluded by name in the mode table and this leg is what checks that.

L5, THE RISK LEG, AND THE ONE WORTH FAILING. Blend_surface/* bit-identical, all 35. The claim is that the write side reproduces exactly what the read-side swizzle was delivering on this suite: the goldens' O-vs-Z difference is exactly 65,536 px on each DstAlpha capture -- eight half-swatches, 8192 px each, all inside swatch rectangles -- and the Add_SrcA_DstA pairs' O and Z goldens differ on 38 px, which is label text. So nothing this suite displays is fed by a surface texel the raster never wrote, and the stamp should land on precisely the pixels the swizzle used to cover. THE WORLD IN WHICH IT FAILS is concrete and is this issue's own least-certain point: this arm does NOT change the clear path, and pgraph_get_clear_color returns alpha 1.0 for every pad format. That coincides with the write-side constant for an O surface and contradicts it for a Z one. If any displayed pixel here is fed by a surface texel that the CLEAR wrote and the geometry did not, the four X_Z rows regress by exactly that area and the answer is that the clear stamps too -- which would then be MEASURED rather than assumed. Whichever way it goes, this leg is the experiment on the clear.

L6, COLLATERAL. Surface_clip/*, Texture_DXT/* and Texture_format/* bit-identical. Surface_clip renders R5G6B5 and carries #59 arm 1's 1,175,741 -> 0, so it cannot see this change at all; Texture_DXT and Texture_format draw to the A8R8G8B8 framebuffer and were the two suites the earlier address-keyed and extent-keyed readback scopings broke (448 -> 65,536 with status blank, and 16,096 -> 91,757), which makes them the right tripwire for a change that deletes that scoping outright.

NOT REGISTERED AS LEGS, AND SAID SO RATHER THAN OMITTED. Three quantities are expected to MOVE and the tool cannot express "must not regress", so they are reported rather than bound:
  * Surface_format/Fmt_X1R5G5B5_{Z,O}1R5G5B5, at 29,881 and 16,096 when last measured. They carry the write-side defect in the open, one-directional and in opposite directions -- 10,776 px of green exactly +128 on the Z capture and 3,681 px of green exactly -128 on the O capture, because we store the combiner's alpha where the format's constant belongs. They should shed those and keep whatever else they carry. Registering 19,105 and 12,415 would be registering an ATTRIBUTION, which is a model formed before the fix, and this file has already watched one of those fail a correct change by four times.
  * Texture_render_target/TexFmt_X8R8G8B8 and TexFmt_X1R5G5B5 and their _L twins. They render into a pad-format surface and then sample it, so they are in the blast radius; direction unknown, because whether the old scoping was reaching them is not established.
  * Clear/SCF_X8R8G8B8_{Z,O}8R8G8B8, SCF_X1R5G5B5_O1R5G5B5 and SFC_X1R5G5B5_Z1R5G5B5. Expected inert because the clear path is untouched; if they move, the SCF tests draw as well as clear and L5's world is live.

LIVENESS, so that a set of held legs cannot be vacuous. L1 is the liveness proof: it demands a 59,183 px capture reach 0, which no inert build can do. If L1 fails at a value near 59,183 the stamp never fired and every other leg here is uninformative; if it fails at some other value the stamp fired and the model is wrong. Those are different diagnoses and the number separates them.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLAIM. It does not touch the clear path, the X1A7R8G8B8 requantisation, or the GL renderer's own readback. It does not claim the four files were needed atomically -- that wall was a territory request, and this arm is the measurement of how many of them the fix actually needs.
